statement: The function returns a result r. Define an integer capacity c to be feasible if there exist an integer k and indices 0 = p[0] < p[1] < ... < p[k] = len(weights) with 1 <= k <= days such that for every j with 1 <= j <= k, the sum of weights[i] over all i with p[j-1] <= i < p[j] is at most c. Then for every integer c in the range of Std.I64, capacity c is feasible if and only if r <= c.
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail, panic, overflow, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, capacity r is feasible: there exist an integer k and indices 0 = p[0] < p[1] < ... < p[k] = len(weights) with 1 <= k <= days such that for every j with 1 <= j <= k, the sum of weights[i] over all i with p[j-1] <= i < p[j] is at most r.
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, no smaller capacity is feasible: for every integer c in the range of Std.I64 with c < r, there do not exist an integer k and indices 0 = p[0] < p[1] < ... < p[k] = len(weights) with 1 <= k <= days such that every block sum over p[j-1] <= i < p[j] is at most c.
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), weights[i] <= r. Equivalently, r is at least the maximum package weight.
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the sum of all weights[i] for 0 <= i < len(weights).
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, days * r is at least the sum of all weights[i] for 0 <= i < len(weights). Equivalently, r >= ceiling(total_weight / days), where total_weight is the sum of all weights[i].
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= M * ceiling(len(weights) / days), where M is the maximum of weights[i] over 0 <= i < len(weights).
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and days = 1, r equals the sum of all weights[i] for 0 <= i < len(weights).
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and days = len(weights), r equals the maximum of weights[i] over 0 <= i < len(weights).
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and there is an integer w such that weights[i] = w for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), then r = w * ceiling(len(weights) / days).
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices a and b with 0 <= a < b <= len(weights) such that r equals the sum of weights[i] over all i with a <= i < b.
preconditions: 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever ship_within_days(weights, d1) returns r1 and ship_within_days(weights, d2) returns r2, we have r2 <= r1.
preconditions: For every weights and every d1 and d2 such that 1 <= d1 <= d2 <= len(weights) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weights), 1 <= weights[i] <= 500.

statement: Whenever ship_within_days(weights, days) returns r and ship_within_days(rev, days) returns r_rev, we have r = r_rev.
preconditions: For every weights and days satisfying 1 <= days <= len(weights) <= 50000 and every weights[i] in [1,500]; let rev be the array of length len(weights) with rev[i] = weights[len(weights)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(weights).

statement: Whenever ship_within_days(weights, days) returns r and ship_within_days(weights2, days) returns r2, we have r <= r2.
preconditions: For every two arrays weights and weights2 of the same length n with 1 <= days <= n <= 50000, all entries of weights and weights2 in [1,500], and weights[i] <= weights2[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n.
